report.summary: Two critical correctness bugs found: (1) The _num function definition is incomplete, causing SyntaxError and blocking module import. (2) In price_call(), variable 'untrusted_endpoint' is only defined when host is not None; if host is None, a NameError occurs at the subscription check. Additionally, the Ledger class is absent from the slice, making it impossible to verify the core reservation/atomicity invariants promised in the docstring.
risks: Module unimportable due to syntax error in _num function.
price_call raises NameError when called without explicit host, crashing any budget check that relies on the default host=None path.
Core correctness of budget enforcement (Ledger.reserve, atomic replace on Windows) not visible; no assurance that the check-before-call invariant holds.
Subscription vendor handling may silently widen the cap if not thoroughly tested, but no tests seen.
todos: Fix incomplete _num function (complete the raise statement with an appropriate BudgetError).
Add 'else: untrusted_endpoint = False' in price_call to handle host=None.
Provide the full implementation of Ledger class for a complete audit.
Write a regression test for price_call with host=None to catch the NameError.

handoff.suggestion: Complete the _num function definition to avoid SyntaxError. In price_call, define untrusted_endpoint = False before the if host is not None block so it's always defined. Also, consider adding a default clause after the host block for safety. The Ledger class is missing; its reserve/settle/atomic write logic must be reviewed for Windows compatibility and fail-closed guarantees.
